questions.subject: Physics
questions.stem: [MULTI-CORRECT: +4 / -2 with +3/+2/+1 Partial Marking] A uniform thin rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ rests on a smooth horizontal tabletop. A horizontal impulse $J$ is applied perpendicular to the rod at a distance $x = \frac{L}{6}$ from its center $O$. Which of the following statements is/are correct immediately after the impulse?
options: The center of mass velocity is $v_{\text{cm}} = \frac{J}{M}$
The angular velocity about the center of mass is $\omega = \frac{2J}{ML}$
The instantaneous axis of rotation lies at distance $\frac{L}{2}$ from center $O$ on the opposite side
The kinetic energy imparted to the rod is $\frac{2J^2}{3M}$
questions.explanation: By linear impulse-momentum, $v_{\text{cm}} = J/M$. By angular impulse about $O$, $J(L/6) = (\frac{1}{12}ML^2)\omega \implies \omega = \frac{2J}{ML}$. Distance to instantaneous center $r_{\text{IC}} = v_{\text{cm}}/\omega = L/2$. Kinetic energy $K = \frac{1}{2}Mv_{\text{cm}}^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{J^2}{2M} + \frac{J^2}{6M} = \frac{2J^2}{3M}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Werner’s Theory, IUPAC, VBT, Crystal Field Theory (CFT) & Isomerism
questions.stem: [MATRIX MATCH] Match each coordination species in List-I with its correct hybridization and magnetic nature in List-II:
questions.explanation: $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$ is square planar ($dsp^2$, diamagnetic); $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is tetrahedral ($sp^3$, 2 unpaired electrons); $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is inner-orbital octahedral ($d^2sp^3$, diamagnetic); $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ is outer-orbital octahedral ($sp^3d^2$, 4 unpaired electrons).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Matrices, Determinants, Adjoint Properties & Cramer’s Linear Systems
questions.paragraphPassage: Let $A$ be a $3 \times 3$ non-singular real matrix satisfying $\det(A) = 2$. Define $B = \text{adj}(\text{adj}(A))$.
questions.stem: Based on the passage above, the value of $\det(B^{-1})$ is:
questions.explanation: For an $n \times n$ matrix $A$, $\det(\text{adj}(\text{adj}(A))) = (\det A)^{(n-1)^2}$. With $n = 3$ and $\det A = 2$, $\det(B) = 2^{(3-1)^2} = 2^4 = 16$. Therefore $\det(B^{-1}) = \frac{1}{16}$.
